newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU 97/98 INTVN GRAIN STOCKS SEEN REACHING 11 MLN T.
newsitem.headline: EU 97/98 INTVN GRAIN STOCKS SEEN REACHING 11 MLN T.

text.p: A huge harvest is expected to enlarge EU cereals intervention stocks to 11 million tonnes by the end of 1997/98 (July/June), from 2.3 million last season, the European Commission's agriculture directorate said.

In a report on the outlook for cereals, oilseeds and protein crops in view of EU expansion eastwards, the Commission's agricultural experts forecast a progressive increase in stocks due to international curbs on subsidised exports and higher yields.
Tonnages are seen climbing to 14.3 million tonnes in 2001/2002 and to 58 million -- including 46 million tonnes of wheat -- by 2005/2006.
Cereals production is forecast at 202 million tonnes in 2001/2002 and 214 million in 2005/2006, despite a 17.5 percent set-aside rate.
However, the Commission proposed in July reducing the rate to zero from 2000, which would imply much higher production.
Average cereals yields are expected to rise to 5.89 tonnes per hectare in 2005/2006, from 5.46 tonnes in 1996/97. Soft wheat yields are seen climbing to 7.21 tonnes, from 6.53.

Cereals consumption is projected growing to 177.9 million tonnes in 2005/2006, from 169.6 million in 1996/97. It includes a four million tonne increase, mostly in wheat, to 109 million tonnes in the use of cereals in animal feed.
Total oilseeds production is expected to grow moderately to 12.8 million tonnes in 2005/2006, from 12.2 million in 1996/97. Average yields are seen little changed at around 2.3 tonnes per hectare.
Protein crops are likely to be stable at 4.5 million tonnes.
The oilseed and protein production forecasts, which were based on a 17.5 percent set-aside rate, could both prove conservative.

The report is the fourth in a series on the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) 2000, comprising a general overview of market trends and beef and milk studies. It will be followed by a study on rural development.
